newsitem.title: EGYPT: BOXING-EUBANK OUTCLASSES BARRERA IN COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-EUBANK OUTCLASSES BARRERA IN COMEBACK.

text.p: Britain's flamboyant former world champion Chris Eubank stopped Argentine Louis Barrera in the fifth of a scheduled 10 rounds in Cairo on Saturday in an uninspiring and one-sided return from retirement.
Barrera, a former South American champion who had lost his last four bouts, was no physical match for Eubank although it was the first fight for the British boxer in a year.

The stadium, filled to almost half its 24,000-seat capacity by army soldiers and policemen, whistled and jeered as the two pranced around each other for four rounds without doing any significant damage.

But Eubank, world super-middleweight champion in 1990 and 1991, seemed to perk up by the end of the fourth and almost one minute into the fifth he hammered the Argentine's head and side, sending him tumbling to the floor.
"No doubt he (Eubanks) was holding back, trying to make the most of the publicity he was getting... it was not much of a match, it was quite ridiculous," one spectator commented.

Flanked by state security officers, Eubank -- nicknamed "Simply the Best" -- had marched into the arena to wild cheering from an Egyptian audience which included Gamal, the son of President Hosni Mubarak.

The fight, dubbed "Style on the Nile" by the Eubank camp and held under the auspices of the World Boxing Organisation, was reportedly heavily sponsored by the boxer himself. The Egyptian daily Al-Ahram was the other main sponsor.
Eubank told reporters on Friday that he was hoping his comeback fight would show Egyptians the "nobility of boxing and how it is a metaphor for life and success".
